history: Credited to Tujague’s in New Orleans, where it won a 1918 cocktail competition in New York. It became a supper-club fixture and then a punchline; it is better than its reputation.
whyItWorks: Equal parts is the whole trick: neither liqueur wins, and the cream rounds both into something closer to ice cream than a cocktail.
steps: Shake all three hard with ice—harder and longer than a sour, to aerate the cream.
Grate nutmeg over the top and add a mint sprig.
techniqueNotes: Green crème de menthe is traditional and gives the color; white makes a paler, less garish drink.
Half-and-half thins it out. Use real heavy cream.

substitutions.notes: A splash of Irish cream in place of dairy makes a richer, sweeter version.

name: Grasshopper
description: Mint, chocolate and cream in equal thirds—New Orleans dessert in a coupe.
